name: Iceland
tagline: One English bachelor's degree in the whole country
summary: Read this part first, because it changes everything else. Across all seven Icelandic universities there is exactly one bachelor's degree that is verifiably taught entirely in English: International Studies in Education, BA at the University of Iceland. Every other bachelor's programme in Iceland is taught in Icelandic, and several explicitly demand Icelandic proficiency or refuse applications from abroad altogether. Iceland is a realistic destination for an exchange semester or a master's degree. It is not, in 2027, a realistic place to do an undergraduate degree in English.
whyConsider: As an EEA citizen you pay no tuition at six of the seven universities — just a registration fee of ISK 100,000 a year, about 720 euros.
The one English-taught bachelor's, International Studies in Education, is a real 180-ECTS degree capped at 60 students with about 30 international places, so the cohort is small.
Danish SU travels here on Nordic terms: the full programme length plus up to twelve extra months, rather than the four-year cap that applies outside the Nordics.
Danish students face no English test at all. The University of Iceland's IB page says English proficiency is 'Not required' for IB Diploma holders.
Nordic citizens get the simplest possible healthcare position — confirmation of home insurance is enough — and register domicile through a separate Nordic track.
watchOuts: One English-taught bachelor's degree nationally. Reykjavik University's own programme filter returns zero results for undergraduate plus English. Akureyri, Bifröst and the Agricultural University teach bachelor's degrees in Icelandic only.

The University of Iceland begins charging tuition to non-EEA students in autumn 2027 — that is this exact cohort. Students starting in autumn 2026 are explicitly exempt. The amount per ECTS has not been set.

For international applicants the University of Iceland deadline is 1 February, a full six months before you start. Two of its own pages disagree about whether Danish citizens can instead use the 5 June Nordic deadline, so apply by 1 February and email admission@hi.is to check.
No minimum IB point score is published by any Icelandic university. The '27 points' figure that circulates online is from commercial aggregator sites, not from any official page.

Reykjavik University publishes undergraduate tuition of ISK 1,794,000 a year for non-EEA students while its bachelor teaching is in Icelandic and one department says it does not accept applications from abroad. Email admissions@ru.is before assuming any English route exists.
Living costs are Copenhagen-level or above. A realistic floor is around ISK 184,000 a month, and Reykjavík's official minimum-support benchmark is ISK 247,572.

ibRecognition.gradeConversion: The IB Diploma is treated as equivalent to the Icelandic stúdentspróf. The IBO's recognition database records the University of Iceland as accepting it 'as Icelandic general High School diploma'. No points-to-grade table is published.
notes: The University of Iceland is the only Icelandic institution with a dedicated IB page. It confirms the Diploma is accepted, that no translation of documents is needed, and that no separate English proficiency evidence is needed.
The IB Career-Related Programme is explicitly rejected. Only the full Diploma counts.
No minimum point score is published anywhere, and subject requirements are set faculty by faculty rather than centrally. Do not rely on any number you find on an aggregator site.

Reykjavik University, Akureyri, Bifröst, the Agricultural University, Hólar and the Iceland University of the Arts do not name the IB anywhere in their admissions material. Their formal position on it is unknown.
Whether IB English A and English B are treated differently is not addressed by any Icelandic university.
Medicine, odontology and physical therapy at the University of Iceland have entrance exams in June; nursing, dental technology and odontology have exams in December. These are taught in Icelandic.
Request your transcript through the IB website and have it sent to transcript@hi.is.

portal.name: None. Study in Iceland states there is no central admissions system — you apply directly to each university. Háskólanám.is is a programme catalogue only.

deadlines.label: University of Iceland, international applicants (undergraduate and master's)
deadlines.year: recurring annual date; 2027-specific dates not yet published
deadlines.notes: Published as "1 February" with no year; the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. Supporting documents due the same day. The application period opens in mid-December. This is the safe deadline for a Danish applicant.

deadlines.label: Reykjavik University, EU/EEA residents, autumn
deadlines.notes: Published as "30 April" with no year; the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. Applications open 5 February. Non-EU/EEA applicants have a much earlier deadline of 31 January and are admitted to the autumn semester only.

deadlines.label: University of Iceland, Icelandic and Nordic citizens, undergraduate autumn start
deadlines.notes: Published as "5 June" with no year; the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. The deadline page lists this as open to Nordic citizens, which would include Danes. The FAQ page instead frames it as being for international students already legally resident in Iceland. The two official pages conflict — apply by 1 February and confirm with admission@hi.is.

deadlines.label: University of Akureyri, EU/EEA and Icelandic applicants
deadlines.notes: Published as "5 June" with no year; the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. The window opens at the beginning of March. Non-EEA applicants must apply by 1 March for Polar Law and 1 April for everything else, and pay a 50-euro application fee.

deadlines.label: Registration fee payment, University of Iceland and Akureyri
deadlines.notes: Published as "4 July" with no year; the year here is inferred from the intake this profile covers. Late payment carries a 15 percent surcharge. The fee is non-refundable with no exemptions.

steps: Accept early that your realistic target is one programme: International Studies in Education, BA at the University of Iceland. Check its page before you plan anything else.
Apply directly to the university — there is no central portal and no way to apply to several institutions on one form.
Get your application in by 1 February 2027, with all supporting documents the same day. Do not assume the June Nordic deadline applies to you.
Ask your IB coordinator to send your transcript to transcript@hi.is through the IB's own service.
If the programme is oversubscribed past its 60-place cap, selection looks at prior higher education, work experience in education, your CV and a personal statement — so write the statement properly.
Pay the ISK 100,000 registration fee by 4 July 2027. It is non-refundable.
Apply for student housing through studentagardar.is the moment you are admitted, and register your domicile with Registers Iceland to get a kennitala once you arrive.
application.selectionNotes: Admission at the University of Iceland is by matriculation examination or equivalent, with requirements varying by faculty. International Studies in Education is capped at 60 students, split roughly 30 international and 30 domestic, and if oversubscribed it ranks on prior study, relevant work experience, CV and personal statement rather than on grades alone. Reykjavik University assesses each applicant individually on grades, further education, work experience, extracurricular participation and stated interests, and requires two references on institutional letterhead plus a letter of intent of at most 300 words.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: One, verified: International Studies in Education, BA at the University of Iceland, 180 ECTS over three years, whose page states that all teaching is in English. The University of Iceland publishes no list of English-taught bachelor's degrees, so treat one as a verified floor rather than a certainty. Reykjavik University, Akureyri, Bifröst and the Agricultural University have none. The Iceland University of the Arts and Hólar do not publish a language of instruction, so theirs is unknown.
language.englishProof: Not required at all if you hold an IB Diploma — the University of Iceland's IB page says so directly. Its Denmark page also accepts a Danish studentereksamen, HHX or HTX with English. Reykjavik University, for its English-taught graduate provision, asks for TOEFL iBT 91, IELTS Academic 6.5, DAAD B2 or Cambridge B2.
notes: The University of Iceland states plainly that the primary language of instruction is Icelandic and that its English-taught programmes are mostly at graduate level. It runs over 600 English-taught individual courses, but those are for incoming exchange students, not degree-seekers.

Study in Iceland's national portal lists two English-taught bachelor's degrees, but one of them — Icelandic as a Second Language, BA — is actually taught in Icelandic and requires you to pass an admission test at CEFR A2+ Icelandic. Do not treat it as an English-taught option.

Reykjavik University's Computer Science BSc page says: taught in Icelandic, proficiency in Icelandic is a requirement, and applications from abroad are not accepted. Its Business Administration BSc requires Icelandic even though all third-year teaching is in English.
Bifröst requires Icelandic at B2.2 for business and social science and C1.2 for law, plus TOEFL iBT 94.

If you are serious about Iceland, the honest routes are: take the one English BA; learn Icelandic to B2 or C1 first; or do your bachelor's elsewhere and come here for a master's, where English provision is far broader.

tuitionEuEea.value: No tuition at six of the seven universities — only a registration fee of ISK 100,000 per year (about 720 euros), or ISK 75,000 for a spring start. The University of Iceland raised this from ISK 75,000 in February 2026, the first increase since 2014. Reykjavik University is the exception and charges real tuition: ISK 656,000 per year for EEA undergraduates, about 4,726 euros.

tuitionNonEu.value: Reykjavik University charges ISK 1,794,000 per year, about 12,925 euros, for non-EEA undergraduates. The University of Iceland will begin charging non-EEA tuition in autumn 2027 — this cohort — but the amount per ECTS has not been set. The Iceland University of the Arts began charging non-EEA tuition in autumn 2026, also at an unpublished amount.

costs.applicationFee: None for EEA citizens at the University of Iceland. Non-EEA applicants pay a processing fee of ISK 20,000 at the University of Iceland, ISK 16,000 at Reykjavik University (covering two applications, deducted from tuition if admitted), 135 euros at Bifröst and 50 euros at Akureyri. The Iceland University of the Arts charges ISK 5,000 per application to everyone.

livingCostMonthly.value: A realistic floor of about ISK 184,000 per month excluding books, roughly 1,326 euros. Reykjavík City's official minimum support benchmark is ISK 247,572, about 1,784 euros. Housing with utilities starts at ISK 100,000, food at ISK 56,000, transport at ISK 6,000.
livingCostMonthly.year: undated — the University of Iceland does not state which year these figures are for

notes: Exchange rate used throughout: 1 euro = 138.80 ISK, taken from the Central Bank of Iceland on 22 September 2026. The Bank's page did not date the rate, so treat conversions as indicative.
Registration fees are service fees, not tuition. They cover services beyond teaching and are non-refundable with no exemptions.
Bifröst abolished tuition entirely and now charges only the ISK 100,000 admission and registration fee, with exam fees billed separately.

Student housing at Stúdentagarðar ranges from ISK 109,755 for an unfurnished 24 square metre room to about ISK 187,461 for a central studio. Electricity, heating and laundry are included in most houses. Base rents rose 2 percent in September 2025 and 5.25 percent in September 2026, so budget for annual increases.

funding: Danish SU for a full degree abroad, at DKK 7,426 a month before tax for students living away from home in 2026. Because Iceland is a Nordic country, SU covers the prescribed programme length plus up to twelve extra months rather than the four-year cap that applies elsewhere. Apply through minSU Fast Track no later than the first month you want support for, and document your progress twice a year.

Menntasjóður námsmanna, the Icelandic student loan fund, appears to be directly open to you. Its rules list being a citizen of Denmark, Finland, Norway or Sweden as a standalone qualifying condition, with no work or residency requirement attached — unlike other EEA citizens, who must work at least 40 hours a month in Iceland. This is more generous than most Nordic funds, so confirm it with the fund before relying on it.
You cannot take both. Menntasjóður states that students cannot receive an Icelandic student loan while receiving study assistance from another state, which includes Danish SU. It is one or the other.

Menntasjóður mechanics if you go that route: you must complete at least 22 ECTS per semester, the maximum loan covers 30 ECTS, and the 2026/27 deadlines were 15 October, 15 February and 15 June, with late applications automatically rejected. A housing top-up loan is available if your rent is at least ISK 40,000 a month. A travel loan of ISK 60,000 a year applies to students from Nordic countries.

There is no tuition loan for the registration fee. Menntasjóður does not lend for the first ISK 100,000 of annual tuition, which is exactly what the registration fee costs — so at the University of Iceland, Akureyri, Bifröst and the arts university there is no tuition loan at all.

Scholarships are close to non-existent at bachelor level. The University of Iceland states in the IBO database that it offers no scholarships to any students. The Icelandic Government Scholarships administered by the Árni Magnússon Institute are only for studying Icelandic language, literature and history.
workRights: EEA citizens, including Danes, need no work permit in Iceland. Non-EEA students need a work permit, and the weekly hour limit could not be verified on any official page.
residency: As a Nordic citizen you have a separate, simpler track with Registers Iceland (Þjóðskrá) rather than the Directorate of Immigration. You are entitled to apply for legal domicile registration if you intend to stay three months or longer, and required to if you stay six months or longer. Registering gets you a kennitala, the Icelandic ID number, which you need for a bank account, a housing contract and health registration. Non-EEA students need a student residence permit costing ISK 70,000, applied for by 1 July for the autumn semester, and usually granted six months at a time.
housing: Student housing for University of Iceland students is run by Félagsstofnun stúdenta through studentagardar.is. Applications are accepted year-round, and new students starting in the autumn can apply from 1 May — though one FS page says 1 June and another says 1 May, so check both. FS publishes no waiting-list data. Reykjavík's private rental market is tight and expensive, so apply the day you are admitted. Rent includes electricity, heating and, in most houses, laundry. Reykjavik University publishes no student housing information.
healthcare: As a Nordic student you have the easiest position of anyone: Study in Iceland says Nordic students need only confirmation of insurance in their home country, such as a health insurance card. Bring your Danish EHIC and present it with your passport at medical visits. There is a widely repeated claim that Icelandic Health Insurance only begins after six months of legal domicile. That could not be confirmed on any official page, though the fact that Menntasjóður lends up to ISK 550,000 a year for health insurance costs suggests a real gap exists. Non-EU students must have insurance in place before arrival.

institutions.name: University of Iceland
institutions.englishBachelors: 1 verified — International Studies in Education, BA (180 ECTS, capped at 60 students). The university publishes no list, so one is a floor rather than a certainty.
institutions.note: Iceland's oldest and largest university, around 14,000 students across five schools, and the only one with a dedicated IB page. It is also the only place in the country with a verified English-taught bachelor's degree. Non-EEA students starting in autumn 2027 will be the first cohort ever charged tuition here.

institutions.name: Reykjavik University
institutions.englishBachelors: None. RU's own programme filter, set to undergraduate plus taught in English, returns no results. Individual programme pages state 'Taught in Icelandic. Proficiency in Icelandic is a requirement.'
institutions.note: Iceland's largest private university and the only one charging real tuition, yet every bachelor's degree is taught in Icelandic — and the Computer Science department states outright that applications from abroad are not accepted. Its English-language admissions machinery is aimed at master's students. Email admissions@ru.is before assuming otherwise.

institutions.name: University of Akureyri
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Study in Iceland states that Polar Law is the only full-time programme taught in English at Akureyri, and Polar Law is a master's.
institutions.note: Iceland's second university, in the capital of the north, with around 2,850 students and about half of them studying at a distance. Its Arctic and polar law specialism is genuinely distinctive — but that is a master's, and there is no English-taught bachelor's here.

institutions.name: Bifröst University
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Bifröst states that the primary language of instruction is Icelandic, with a selection of individual courses in English. Non-Icelandic speakers need Icelandic at B2.2 for business and social science, C1.2 for law.
institutions.note: A small rural university in west Iceland, founded on the model of Ruskin College, Oxford, and heavily online. It has abolished tuition entirely and now charges only the ISK 100,000 registration fee. But no full bachelor's degree is available in English. Its application deadlines could not be verified.

institutions.name: Agricultural University of Iceland
institutions.englishBachelors: None. Its own page states the language of instruction is Icelandic, only occasionally English or Scandinavian, though most textbooks are in English or Scandinavian languages.
institutions.note: Five bachelor's degrees of 180 ECTS each, including equine science and landscape architecture, which are hard to find elsewhere — but all taught in Icelandic. Entry expects level 2 natural sciences, level 3 English and level 2 mathematics alongside a matriculation examination. Fees and deadlines could not be verified.

institutions.name: Iceland University of the Arts
institutions.note: The only university-level arts degrees in Iceland — thirteen bachelor's programmes covering architecture, fine art, fashion and product design, film, acting, dance and music, with around 600 students. It does not publish a language of instruction for any of them, so whether any is taught in English is unknown. It started charging tuition to non-EEA students in autumn 2026 at an unpublished amount, and charges ISK 5,000 per application. Portfolio or audition requirements are likely but unconfirmed.

institutions.name: Hólar University
institutions.note: A tiny specialist university on the site of a cathedral school dating to 1106, with three niches you will not find together anywhere else: fish biology, horses and tourism. It appears to have been absorbed into the University of Iceland — checked again 2026-09-23, holar.is and holar.is/en/ both redirect to hi.is, which presents it as "Háskóli Íslands á Hólum" inside the HÍ consortium, and Hólar has no site of its own left — but the national portals still list it separately and the effective date and legal form of that merger could not be confirmed. Its fees, deadlines and language of instruction are all unverified.
